text: 5-year-old boy. The patient is presented by his mother for a well-child visit. speaker: Doctor
text: DIAGNOSIS READY: Pheochromocytoma (unlikely given lack of classic symptoms like episodic headache, sweating, and tachycardia); more likely benign causes of secondary hypertension in a 5-year-old such as renal artery stenosis, renal parenchymal disease, or coarctation of the aorta.
